collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 40 or older)

collection.description: A villager remembers the one choice that turned out right, a fruit tree by the path: go and look at it, or stay in the hammock.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (name1) has made plenty of mistakes in (his/her) life. (He/she) has planted beans in the wrong season, built a wall that fell down twice, and once tried to cook an entire meal using only seawater. But lying in the hammock today, (he/she) remembers one small choice, years ago, that turned out exactly right: (he/she) planted a fruit tree by the path where everyone walks. Every day, people stop and pick from it.

choices.label: Go and Look at the Tree

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (name1) gets out of the hammock and walks down to the tree. A child is up in the branches, eating. An elder is resting in the shade. A goat is trying to reach the low fruit. (name1) stands there and watches, enormously pleased with (him/her)self, until the goat gets the fruit. (He/she) decides one good thing done well is quite a lot.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) stays in the hammock and lists the other mistakes, just to keep (him/her)self humble. It's a long list. Then (he/she) thinks of the tree again and smiles. It's not a fair trade, a whole list of mistakes for one tree. But (he/she) likes the tree better than (he/she) dislikes the mistakes. (He/she) falls asleep content.

text_only.reason: a feeling in the moment, not a lasting dislike -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only
